costDefShort: the total expenses the charity reports to the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission (ACNC) each year, which can include wear on buildings (depreciation).
defs: Spending: the total expenses Bodhipala Monastery Ltd reports to the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission (ACNC) in its yearly Annual Information Statement; the statement does not separate wear on buildings (depreciation) or the kinds of cost. Residents: the monks, novices, nuns and anagārikas listed at Bodhipala on the community lists, on average; guests and lay residents are not counted. Inflation: the Australian consumer price index (World Bank). All amounts in Australian dollars, as paid at the time, unless the page says "in today's money".
holdLede: The statement also gives what the charity owns and owes at the end of each year.

meaningNote: The statements give totals only, so this page cannot say what the money was spent on.
holdNote: Liabilities are large for a monastery of this size ($0.7 to $0.9 million of the $1.3 to $1.6 million of assets); the statement does not say what they are.
notes: Where the figures come from. Bodhipala Monastery Ltd (Australian business number 76 627 533 475) is a registered charity. Its yearly totals come from the ACNC's published Annual Information Statement data for the years 2017 to 2024 (acnc_ais.csv in this folder keeps the rows for this charity).
Years. The charity's year runs from 1 July to 30 June. It is named by the year it ends in: "2024" is July 2023 to June 2024.

What the statement shows. Total income, total expenses, total assets and total liabilities. It has no cost lines and does not separate wear on buildings (depreciation), so nothing is taken out of spending and this page cannot show what the money went on.
Money in. Total gross income as reported. Some of it can be given for a set purpose, such as building work, which the statement does not show.
First year. The charity registered in July 2018, so the first statement is for the year to June 2019. Bodhipala is described on the forest sangha's lists as a branch of Bodhivana Monastery.
Not in the accounts. Food, and much of the work done for a monastery, is given by supporters and is not a cost line.
Residents are the monks, novices, nuns and anagārikas on the community lists. Guests, retreatants and lay residents are not counted.
